title: Synthesis and Characterization of a New Hybrid Polyoxometalate Compound: Bis(3-aminopropyl)ammonium Hexatungstotellurate(VI) Octahydrate
abstract: Synthesis strategy of hybrids Polyoxometalates have drawn a lot of attention owing to interesting. Herein, we describe, the one pot process used to synthesize a new hybrid polyoxotungstate, (C&lt;sub&gt;6&lt;/sub&gt;H&lt;sub&gt;20&lt;/sub&gt;N&lt;sub&gt;3&lt;/sub&gt;)&lt;sub&gt;2&lt;/sub&gt;[TeW&lt;sub&gt;6&lt;/sub&gt;O&lt;sub&gt;24&lt;/sub&gt;].8H&lt;sub&gt;2&lt;/sub&gt;O, at a temperature of 200°C. This preparation was carried out by mixing equimolar amounts of H&lt;sub&gt;2&lt;/sub&gt;WO&lt;sub&gt;4&lt;/sub&gt;, C&lt;sub&gt;6&lt;/sub&gt;H&lt;sub&gt;17&lt;/sub&gt;N&lt;sub&gt;3&lt;/sub&gt;, and H&lt;sub&gt;6&lt;/sub&gt;TeO&lt;sub&gt;6&lt;/sub&gt;. The compound was characterized by infrared and UV-visible spectroscopy techniques, as well as by X-ray diffraction. The compound crystallizes in the monoclinic system with the space group P2&lt;sub&gt;1&lt;/sub&gt;/c. The unit cell are: a = 8.74874(14) Å, b = 12.5894(2) Å, c = 18.5176(3) Å, α = 90°, β = 92.6078(14)°, γ = 90°. The compound consists of a non-protonated Anderson-type heteropolyanion [TeW&lt;sub&gt;6&lt;/sub&gt;O&lt;sub&gt;24&lt;/sub&gt;]&lt;sup&gt;6-&lt;/sup&gt; stabilized by two organoammonium cations [C&lt;sub&gt;6&lt;/sub&gt;H&lt;sub&gt;20&lt;/sub&gt;N&lt;sub&gt;3&lt;/sub&gt;]&lt;sup&gt;3+&lt;/sup&gt; and eight water molecules. The polyoxoanion [TeW&lt;sub&gt;6&lt;/sub&gt;O&lt;sub&gt;24&lt;/sub&gt;]&lt;sup&gt;6-&lt;/sup&gt; adopts an Anderson-Evans type structure of class A. Thus, the polyanion is bult of six {WO&lt;sub&gt;6&lt;/sub&gt;} units surrounding a {TeO&lt;sub&gt;6&lt;/sub&gt;} octahedron. The six {WO&lt;sub&gt;6&lt;/sub&gt;} are linked together by edges sharing and connected around the heteroatom, via oxygen atoms, forming a planar structure with approximate D3d symmetry. The cohesion of the three-dimensional structure is ensured by hydrogen bonds between the polyanions, the organoammonium groups, and the water molecules, thereby providing significant stability to the compound. UV–Visible absorption spectroscopy shows a strong absorption band at 296nm attributed to Ligand-Metal Charge Transfer (LMCT) transition of the O→W and the main IR absorption bands of the polyanion appear at: 942 cm⁻¹, 875 cm⁻¹, 766 cm⁻¹ and 599 cm-¹.
